newsitem.title: USA: Gleason Corp. buys Pfauter Group for $36 million.
newsitem.headline: Gleason Corp. buys Pfauter Group for $36 million.

text.p: Gleason Corp. said Monday that it has agreed to acquire cylindrical gear equipment producer Hermann Pfauter Group for about $36 million in cash and the assumption of about $56 million in bank debt.

The deal includes Hermann Pfauter GmbH & Co., a leading gear equipment producer based in Ludwigsburg, Germany; Pfauter's 76 percent interest in Pfauter-Maag Cutting Tools, a cutting tool maker in Loves Park, Ill.; and Pfauter-Maag management's 24 percent ownership interest in that company.

Gleason, a major maker of gear production equipment, said it will incur one-time costs of about $9 million or $5 million after tax to incorporate Pfauter into its existing operations. "These upfront costs should translate into annual savings of a similar magnitude in approximately 24 months," it said.
Gleason, based in Rochester, N.Y., said it expects the deal to boost its earnings within a year.

The acquisition will be funded through syndicated bank financing led by Chase Manhattan Bank with a new multi-currency facility of up to $170 million. Regulatory approvals in Germany and the United States have been granted, it said.

The Pfauter Group, with operations in Germany, Italy and the United States, manufactures gear cutting machinery for production of cylindrical gears. It employs more than 1,000 people and had 1996 sales of about $175 million.
Gleason's stock rose $1 cents to $45 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange at midafternoon.
